title: A Bayesian Network analysis: how do distinguished scholars enhance the innovation performance?
abstract: The resources and capabilities of distinguished scholars are dynamically matched with the external environment, contributing to the continuous output of innovative knowledge and promoting the effective improvement of scholars’ innovation performance. This paper proposes a big data-driven analysis method and establishes a framework for distinguished scholars based on the three dimensions of environment, individual, and collaborative resources, incorporating six characteristic variables, including innovative atmosphere, extrinsic motivation, knowledge producing, scientific research efficacy, breadth of collaboration, and depth of collaboration. Next, using K-Means clustering, distinguished scholars are categorized into three heterogeneous groups, including motivational, platform-based, and collaborative groups. Finally, Bayesian Networks are constructed for each group to uncover the influence mechanism between characteristic variables and knowledge innovation performance, thereby providing personalized development strategies for distinguished scholars to achieve high-performance goals. The findings reveal that Heterogeneous groups of distinguished scholars exhibit distinct Bayesian network structures, with significantly different impact pathways of characteristic variable combinations on performance. Moreover, knowledge producing serves as a core driver of knowledge innovation performance, demonstrating universal applicability. Furthermore, resource allocation for collaborative partnerships should be differentiated based on scholar types. The motivational group should maintain a moderate breadth of collaboration, while the collaborative group should further expand collaboration channels to stimulate innovation. This paper points out a variety of possible strategies for heterogeneous distinguished scholars to achieve high performance, and highlights the equal utility effect of different characteristic combinations on scholars’ innovation performance, providing theoretical and behavioral guidance for management departments to implement differentiated performance incentive measures.

title: Cardiovascular medicine preprints: publication rates, citation rates, and time to publication
abstract: Preprints are preliminary reports that have not undergone peer review and have seen exponential growth in health sciences, particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic. Preprints facilitate rapid dissemination and scientific discussion. Their role in cardiovascular medicine, a rapidly advancing field, remains incompletely understood. Evaluate the publication rate and the difference in citation counts and citation rates between preprint and published versions of cardiovascular preprints. We collected cardiovascular preprints from two major preprint servers, medRxiv and Research Square, using data scraping and CrossRef metadata. We determined the publication rate and compared citation counts and citation rates using non-parametric methods between the published preprints and their publication version. Additionally, we analyzed the publication rate, citation counts, citation rates, and time interval from preprint posting to journal publication among preprint servers. Among 5625 preprints, 1837 (32.66%) were published in peer-reviewed journals. Older preprints showed higher cumulative publication rates as of the data extraction date, with 61.50% of preprints from 2019 published compared with 6.36% of preprints from 2024 (p < 0.001). The median time to publication was 154 days, with significant differences between preprint servers (Research Square: 133 days vs. medRxiv: 185 days, p < 0.001). Citation analysis revealed a median of 0 citations for all preprints, with 84.80% having zero citations. Published preprints had significantly higher citation counts than unpublished ones (median 0 vs. 0, p < 0.0001; mean 0.55 vs. 0.25), and published articles had notably more citations than their respective preprints (median 5 vs. 0, p < 0.0001; mean 13.51 vs. 0.55). Published preprints had higher monthly citation rates than unpublished ones, and published articles had higher monthly citation rates than their respective preprints (p <0.0001). A greater proportion of older cardiovascular preprints had transitioned to peer-reviewed publication by the data extraction date. Preprints that are published receive more citations, suggesting that published versions are perceived as more scientifically impactful.

title: A precision-driven evaluation protocol for author name disambiguation
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13415v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Author Name Disambiguation systems are commonly evaluated using pairwise and B$^3$ metrics, which summarize clustering quality through aggregate precision and recall but do not explicitly distinguish between lumping (merging publications from different authors) and splitting (fragmenting the publications of a single author). Because these errors can have asymmetric consequences in bibliographic applications, we propose a precision-driven evaluation framework that decomposes clustering quality into complementary instance-level and cluster-level signals. The framework introduces cluster-level Lumping Error and Splitting Error to separately quantify contamination and fragmentation, combines them with standard pairwise and B$^3$ metrics through a Composite Score, and uses the resulting measures for model selection. We characterize the diagnostic behavior of the framework through a controlled synthetic case study and assess the sensitivity of the Composite Score to its weighting scheme. The results show that the proposed structural measures distinguish error patterns that aggregate metrics can mask, while the sensitivity analysis identifies a stable region for the adopted weighting configuration. The framework is released as an open-source Python pipeline.
thinking: 该论文针对作者姓名消歧系统评估中传统指标无法区分“合并”与“分裂”错误的局限性，提出了一个包含实例级和簇级信号的精确度驱动评估框架，方法设计严谨且进行了敏感性分析。其贡献主要在于评估方法学本身，虽技术前沿性中等，但作为开源工具包对改进消歧系统开发有直接实用价值。

title: OC-AND: A Citation-Enriched Benchmark for Author Name Disambiguation
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13462v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Author Name Disambiguation benchmarks are predominantly derived from closed infrastructures that may not reflect conditions in open bibliographic environments. We present OC-AND, an open citation-enriched benchmark for AND constructed by remapping the WhoIsWho dataset with bibliographic and citation metadata from OpenCitations. The dataset is produced through a reproducible five-stage pipeline involving DOI verification, metadata validation, OpenCitations enrichment, and author-centric transformation. OC-AND retains the WhoIsWho ground-truth files and partition structure unchanged, while its publication files are restricted to publications that could be matched to a validated DOI and an OpenCitations record. It introduces realistic characteristics of open environments: heterogeneous metadata completeness, absent abstracts and affiliations, asymmetric citation coverage, and sparse graph connectivity. The dataset contains author records with associated citations, enabling evaluation of AND methods in settings closer to real-world open scholarly infrastructure scenarios. OC-AND is released as open data with complete provenance documentation and pipeline code, supporting reproducible research and the development of citation-aware disambiguation approaches.
thinking: 该论文构建了一个基于开放引文数据的作者姓名消歧基准数据集，采用了前沿的开放科学基础设施，技术方法具有创新性。数据集构建流程规范、可复现，但作为基准数据集本身，其业务落地价值主要体现在为后续研究提供评估工具，而非直接应用于图书馆或信息机构的日常业务。

title: Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13277v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Memory-augmented assistants retrieve evidence from stored conversations and documents to answer queries. Most embedding-based retrievers compare single-vector representations of queries and memories, even when relevance depends on a small part of the content. Such local evidence can be matched to queries using the contextual token representations already computed by the same embedding models. Our method uses sparse token matching to improve retrieval without additional training. Each query token retrieves a small set of matching tokens across candidate memories. The matching scores are aggregated for each memory and combined with whole-memory similarity to rank memories. An optional low-rank query adapter can be trained with supervision while keeping the encoder and stored memory representations fixed. Our method improves retrieval across eight benchmarks and multiple model families without additional training. Query adaptation further increases the gains to 13.3 and 14.3 percentage points in average Recall@10 and NDCG@10 on Qwen3-Embedding-4B. These retrieval gains translate into higher question-answering accuracy on long-term memory benchmarks.
thinking: 该论文提出了一种基于稀疏令牌匹配的检索增强方法，通过利用嵌入模型已计算的上下文令牌表示来捕捉局部证据，无需额外训练即可提升检索效果，方法新颖且实验验证充分。其技术思路具有前沿性，但作为预印本论文，其方法在具体业务场景（如图书馆问答系统）中的直接落地路径和集成成本尚未充分探讨。
one_sentence_summary: 该研究提出一种无需额外训练的稀疏令牌匹配方法，通过结合局部令牌证据与整体记忆相似性，显著提升了记忆增强问答系统的检索性能。

title: PRIME: Pre-Retrieval Index Modeling Enhancement for Structured Document Retrieval-Real
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-precision retrieval over external knowledge bases is essential for LLM agents to operate effectively. However, existing Information Retrieval (IR) research primarily optimizes query-side retrievers (e.g., ColBERT, BGE) and generators (e.g., Self-RAG, GraphRAG), while reducing corpus-side representation to chunking. This leaves index-side quality an underexplored lever. We propose Pre-Retrieval Index Modeling & Enhancement (PRIME), an index-side optimization framework built on two complementary tracks: an LLM-driven Semantic Restructuring (SR) track that transforms long documents into structured, information-dense sections, and a deterministic Metadata Synthesis (MS) and Hierarchical Retrieval (HR) track that extracts semantic anchors and heading structure for coarse-to-fine section retrieval. Our evaluations show that deterministic metadata matches structure-aware chunking's retrieval quality while cutting embedding computation by 45.8 $\times$ and index vector count by 22.4 $\times$. On top of these gains, Semantic Restructuring (SR) further improves Answer-F1 by 13.7% in full deployment, with characterized quality-fidelity-cost trade-offs. Across QASPER, BRIGHT, and NFCorpus, we further characterize three qualitative regimes that determine whether index-side optimization helps or degrades retrieval, while showing that these index-side effects are neutralized under a strong reranker.
thinking: 该论文提出了一个面向结构化文档检索的索引端优化框架PRIME，通过语义重组和元数据合成等方法，显著提升了检索效率并降低了计算成本。其方法设计严谨，在多个数据集上进行了验证，但作为预印本尚未经过同行评议，且技术方案主要面向特定检索场景，通用性有待进一步验证。
one_sentence_summary: 该研究提出一种通过优化索引结构来提升大语言模型外部知识检索效率与精度的新框架。

title: NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13314v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Memory retrieval aims to identify evidence from stored records to answer a query. Stored records with different factual details may share topics, entities, or events. Such shared contents would make records without the required evidence more likely to receive high similarity scores and outrank the correct evidence. In this paper, we use the information shared by these records to construct local references for query-memory matching. We propose NEighborhood-Aware Residuals (NEAR), a training-free framework that uses these references to construct residual representations that complement the original embeddings. Specifically, each memory derives a reference direction from its neighbors, and each query obtains its reference from a precomputed table. Using these references, NEAR constructs projection residuals for both queries and memories. These residuals are combined with the original embeddings for a single approximate nearest-neighbor search over a fixed memory index. Experiments on eight long-context retrieval benchmarks show consistent improvements across nine embedding models. Downstream evaluations show that NEAR improves question-answering performance.
thinking: 该论文提出了一种训练自由的邻域感知残差框架（NEAR），通过构建局部参考来增强查询与记忆的匹配，在多个长上下文检索基准上验证了其有效性。其方法创新性较强，但作为预印本尚未经过同行评议，且实际应用场景和落地价值有待进一步明确。
one_sentence_summary: 该研究提出一种无需训练的新方法，通过利用存储记录间的共享信息来构建残差表示，从而提升了长文本检索的准确性。

title: SPARQL-LLM in the TEXT2SPARQL 2026 Challenge
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13648v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Querying distributed data represented as Knowledge Graphs (KGs) via SPARQL remains a difficult task, requiring fluency in query syntax, endpoint specifications, and schema details. Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) systems address this by automatically translating natural language into SPARQL, and recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have made this translation increasingly feasible. In this paper, we describe SPARQL-LLM, our open-source KGQA system, in the context of the TEXT2SPARQL 2026 challenge. In this challenge, SPARQL-LLM ranks first overall among eight competing approaches across all datasets, achieving up to 59% higher accuracy than the second-best approach and supporting multilingual question answering in English, German, and Spanish. SPARQL-LLM is publicly released at https://github.com/sib-swiss/sparql-llm and deployed in production over decentralized bioinformatics KGs at https://www.expasy.org/chat.
thinking: 论文聚焦于利用大语言模型（LLM）解决知识图谱问答（KGQA）中的自然语言到SPARQL查询转换难题，技术前沿性突出，并在公开评测中取得了显著的性能优势。其成果以开源系统形式发布并已在生物信息学领域实际部署，业务落地价值明确。然而，作为一篇描述系统参与评测的短文，其研究方法部分（如模型架构、训练数据、评估细节）的严谨性未充分展现，影响了方法严谨性的评分。
one_sentence_summary: 该研究提出的SPARQL-LLM系统，在将自然语言问题转换为知识图谱查询的国际评测中表现最佳，并已应用于生物信息学领域。

title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13810v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are now a standard source of query expansion terms but they hallucinate. They inject non existent entities and off-topic terms that add ranking noise and can hurt strong retrievers. Existing remedies such as corpus grounding, mutual verification and preference alignment treat hallucinated terms as an undifferentiated nuisance to be filtered by agreement heuristics, without a mechanistic account of why a given term appears or a principled criterion for how many terms to keep. We propose Subsequence-Association Filtered, breadth-aware query expansion (SAFE-QE), a training-free, retriever agnostic method that draws on the subsequence-association account of hallucination. We score each candidate expansion term by its corpus conditioned cross-context reproducibility, terms that reappear under randomised query contexts yet lack support in the pseudo-relevant set are flagged as products of dominant hallucinatory associations and down-weighted. Drawing on the characterisation of language generation as a trade-off between consistency (no hallucination) and breadth (coverage), we cast term selection as constrained coverage maximisation over the pseudo-relevant set, keeping a set that is approximately broad but consistent and stable across resampling. We also introduce the Hallucinated Expansion Term Rate, a query side faithfulness metric that counts injected expansion terms no relevant document supports. We evaluate our approach on benchmarked TREC and BEIR collections. Our SAFE-QE is statistically indistinguishable from generative and corpus-steered expansion on nDCG@10 while injecting fewer unsupported terms 4.3 per query against 27.8 for Query2doc and 57.5 for HyDE and on a strong learned sparse retriever, where every expansion method regresses. Faithfulness is therefore available at no measurable cost in ranking quality.
thinking: 该论文针对大语言模型查询扩展中的幻觉问题，提出了基于子序列关联过滤和广度感知选择的SAFE-QE方法，在保持检索性能的同时显著减少了幻觉术语的注入，方法设计具有创新性和理论依据。其不足在于作为arXiv预印本，方法尚未在更广泛的真实图书馆或信息检索系统中得到实践验证，且对伪相关文档集的质量有一定依赖。
one_sentence_summary: 该研究提出一种新方法，能有效识别并减少大语言模型在查询扩展时产生的虚假术语，且不影响检索效果。

title: GeopoliticalQA: Benchmarking Retrieval and Generation over Intelligence Reports
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12617v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports constitute a rich source of expert knowledge and have increasing value in the current political climate, but their heterogeneity and analytical complexity pose challenges for retrieval-augmented question answering. We introduce a benchmark for grounded question answering over 415 open-source geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports, comprising 5,525 document-grounded question-answer pairs spanning factual, inferential, comparative, and risk-oriented questions. We propose a document-aware generation pipeline that profiles reports before generating questions and validate dataset quality through expert annotation and an LLM-as-judge protocol. Using the benchmark, we evaluate 15 retrieval systems and six open-weight LLMs for RAG. We find that models perform similarly on document-level retrieval, while at the harder chunk level retrieval quality is not driven by embedding-model scale: bge-m3, a mid-size open encoder matches an order of magnitude larger ones and outperforms commercial embedding APIs. In contrast, answer generation remains challenging even given the gold evidence, particularly for inferential and risk-oriented questions.
thinking: 该论文构建了一个基于地缘政治情报报告的问答基准数据集，并系统评估了多种检索与生成模型，在数据集构建方法上具有创新性，且对开源与商业模型进行了对比分析。然而，其研究场景（开源情报报告）虽具现实意义，但直接应用于图书馆等机构的业务场景路径尚不明确，方法学部分详实但未涉及大规模用户实验验证。
one_sentence_summary: 该研究创建了一个地缘政治情报问答基准，发现中等规模的嵌入模型在检索任务上可媲美大型商业模型，但复杂推理问题的生成答案仍具挑战性。

title: Locate, Judge, Read: Role-Specialized Tool Agents over a Knowledge-Point Index for Open-Domain Multimodal Document QA
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13128v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Question answering over large heterogeneous document collections requires first finding the right passages and then reading them, yet current retrieval-augmented agents give one model both kinds of tools and let it schedule itself. We present KnowForge, a pipeline separated by job: a hybrid-retrieval knowledge-point index; a Locator agent that can only search; a code-scheduled bridge judge that forces the missing second hop; a typed, size-bounded evidence pool that merges every search's ranking; a Deep Reader agent that can only read text, images and tables; and a synthesizer with a format checker. With a self-hosted Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (3B active), KnowForge reaches F1 47.5 on the full open-domain M3DocVQA (2,441 questions, 3,368 PDFs), +11.0 over the published M3DocRAG system and +7.1 over one-shot retrieve-and-answer on the same index and model, and 53.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash. On MultiHop-RAG it reaches 73.5 accuracy, above the strongest published RAG and GraphRAG results (71.2); on the single-document MMLongBench-Doc it lifts the same model from 34.8 to 47.0, level with GPT-4o reading page images (46.3). Per-job ablations on the full benchmarks attribute the gain: the Deep Reader is worth 3.8, 9.8 and 0 points on the three corpora, tracking how visual each is; merging both agents into one with all tools and twice the rounds loses 1.9 F1 because it keeps searching instead of reading; a round-budget sweep shows a step at four Locator rounds and a plateau beyond; query latency scales with model calls rather than corpus size. We serve the three indexed benchmarks as read-only knowledge bases (free registration) and release all prompts and the runner code: https://github.com/metask-ai/knowforge-bench
thinking: 论文提出了一种基于角色分工的检索增强生成（RAG）框架，通过分离定位（Locator）和深度阅读（Deep Reader）代理，并引入知识点索引和证据池等机制，在多模态文档问答任务上取得了显著性能提升。其方法设计严谨，通过消融实验验证了各模块贡献，但所采用的大语言模型和检索技术本身属于当前主流，而非开创性前沿。
one_sentence_summary: 该研究通过让“定位”和“阅读”两个AI代理分工协作，显著提升了从大量多模态文档中寻找并回答复杂问题的准确率。

title: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13416v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming direct users of the open web. As they take on increasingly complex and information-intensive tasks, effective web access is becoming a core capability for agentic problem solving. Existing approaches have advanced agentic web access through different access models, including search-augmented agents, browser-based agents, and, more recently, filesystem-based agents. Nevertheless, as users expect agents to complete long-horizon, end-to-end tasks, they increasingly need to conduct broad information gathering, perform browser actions, and revisit acquired evidence within a single trajectory. Yet our preliminary analyses reveal that existing access models struggle to meet these demands. They primarily support either information gathering or browser interaction, while combining their capabilities can involve substantial costs or performance trade-offs. To this end, we present Web\$hell, an interface that unifies web access under a single access model. Using a common schema defined by WebContract, WebCompiler compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects. These objects are maintained in WebCache and handled through a shared set of operations, providing agents with consistent, operable, and persistent web access. Through extensive experiments across web search, web navigation, and deep research benchmarks, we show that Web\$hell achieves strong task performance at lower cost. Our results further indicate the importance of interface design for effective web access, with Web\$hell opening new possibilities for more capable and efficient LLM agents on the web.
thinking: 该论文提出了一种统一的Web访问接口Web$hell，通过编译网页为可寻址的信息和动作对象，解决了现有LLM代理在复杂Web任务中信息收集与浏览器交互难以兼顾的问题。方法设计新颖且实验充分，但作为技术原型，其在实际图情业务场景中的直接落地路径尚不明确。
one_sentence_summary: 该研究为大型语言模型代理设计了一个统一接口，使其能更高效、低成本地完成网页信息搜索与交互任务。
